plugins.name: Donor Merchant – Donation Form with Recurring Donations, Stripe and PayPal
plugins.author: Matt McWilliam
plugins.short_description: Free donation plugin for nonprofits, churches and charities: one-time and recurring donations with Stripe and PayPal, donor portal and receipts.
plugins.description:
Donor Merchant is a free donation plugin for WordPress. It gives a nonprofit, church, charity, school, or community group a donation form that takes one-time and recurring donations through Stripe and PayPal, keeps a record of every donor and gift in your own database, and sends receipts.

Try the live demo: pick an amount, choose monthly, cover the fees, and see the receipt. Nothing is charged.

Every feature is in the free plugin. There are no paid add-ons, no locked settings, and no fee added on top of what Stripe or PayPal charge. Optional paid support plans are available: priority email help for a single organization, or faster help for agencies looking after several client sites. Details are at donormerchant.com/pricing.

Who it is for

  • Small nonprofits and charities that need a dependable donation page without a monthly platform bill.
  • Churches taking online tithes and offerings, with funds such as General, Building, or Missions, and year-end giving statements donors can download themselves.
  • Schools, PTAs, booster clubs, animal rescues, and community groups running a goal-based campaign.
  • Freelancers and agencies who build sites for nonprofit clients and want one donation setup they can repeat on every site, with no license keys.

Donations

  • One-time and recurring donations. Donors choose one-time, weekly, every 2 weeks, monthly, quarterly, or yearly, and you pick which of those your form offers. Recurring giving works on both gateways: Stripe subscriptions and PayPal subscriptions.
  • Stripe through Stripe’s Payment Element: cards, plus Apple Pay and Google Pay where you have them turned on in your Stripe account.
  • Bank debit (ACH) from US bank accounts through Stripe, as a setting you switch on.
  • PayPal Smart Buttons for one-time gifts.
  • 20 currencies, with WooCommerce-style number formatting: currency position, thousand and decimal separators, and number of decimals, used on the form, receipts, statements, and reports.
  • Suggested amounts and a minimum. Your own suggested amounts, a custom amount field, and a minimum donation the server enforces.
  • Fee recovery. Donors can choose to add the processing fee to their gift, worked out from the percentage and fixed fee you enter so that the full gift is left after the processor’s cut. A donor who pays a one-time gift by bank account is asked for the lower bank fee instead.
  • Designations. Donors pick the fund their gift supports.
  • Tributes. A gift can be made in honor of or in memory of someone, with an optional message.
  • Employer matching. An optional question asks whether the donor’s employer matches gifts. The employer shows on the donation, your new-donation email and the donor’s receipt.
  • Custom fields. Add your own questions as text, paragraph, dropdown, or checkbox fields, each required or optional.
  • Test mode. Test end to end with Stripe test keys and the PayPal sandbox before going live.

Gift Aid for UK charities

Offer Gift Aid on the form when your currency is pounds sterling. Donors tick HMRC’s model declaration (unticked by default) and give a house name or number and postcode, or a full address if they live outside the UK. One declaration covers future gifts and gifts in the past 4 years, so monthly donors are covered. The declaration is stored exactly as the donor saw it.

Donor Merchant > Gift Aid lists the gifts ready to claim and downloads them in HMRC’s schedule format, ready to paste into HMRC’s spreadsheet for Charities Online. Mark gifts as claimed so they are never claimed twice, see refunds that need reporting back, and cancel a declaration when a donor asks. Donors can also cancel from the donor portal.

Campaigns and goal thermometers

Create as many campaigns as you need, each with its own goal, description, suggested amounts, and an optional end date after which its form stops taking gifts. A campaign’s form shows progress toward the goal, and the [donor_merchant_progress campaign="N"] shortcode places the same thermometer anywhere else on your site.

Donor records and reports

  • Every donor and gift is saved in your WordPress database, with each donor’s lifetime total and last donation date.
  • A dashboard shows total raised, this month’s total, number of donations and donors, recurring gifts, and the average gift.
  • Search and filter the donations list by status, and export donations or donors to CSV.
  • Record offline gifts (check, cash, bank transfer, or other) so your totals stay complete, or let donors choose “check or bank transfer” on the form: they get your instructions, and you mark the gift received when it arrives.
  • Add a donor by hand, and correct a gift’s status to completed, refunded, or failed without deleting it. Corrections never email the donor.
  • An optional monthly fundraising summary is emailed to you on the first of each month.

Receipts, statements, and the donor portal

  • Email customization like WooCommerce’s: every email the plugin sends (donation receipt, recurring gift receipt, offline gift instructions, failed recurring payment, new-donation alert, donor portal link and monthly summary) can be switched on or off, given its own subject, heading and message with placeholders such as {first_name}, {amount} and {designation}, and sent as HTML or plain text. Add your logo, colors, font and footer, set the From name and address, preview each email live on desktop or mobile, and send yourself a test.
  • A printable receipt for every gift, showing your organization’s address, tax ID, and your own receipt wording. Donors save it as a PDF from their browser, so no PDF library is bundled.
  • Annual giving statements for the current and previous year.
  • A donor portal with passwordless sign-in by one-time email link, where donors see their giving history, open receipts and statements, cancel any recurring gift and update the card on a Stripe one, with no setup needed in Stripe. Receipts for recurring gifts link to the portal, and you can also cancel a donor’s recurring gift from the Donations list.

Donation importer

The built-in donation importer reads a CSV export and recognizes the exports from GiveWP, Charitable, Donorbox, PayPal, Stripe, WooCommerce, Gravity Forms, and WPForms. Any other spreadsheet works too.

You confirm which column is which before anything is written, and a preview shows the result first. Re-running is safe: gifts already on file are matched by transaction ID, or by donor, amount, and date. Imported gifts never send receipts or fire integrations, and rows marked as test mode can be skipped. Each file can hold up to 10,000 rows.

Integrations

  • Mailchimp. Add donors to an audience, with a “keep me updated” checkbox on the form and optional double opt-in.
  • Outgoing webhooks. Send completed donations to Zapier, Make, a CRM, or your own code. Each request is signed with HMAC-SHA256 so the receiver can confirm it came from your site.

Design and placement

  • A Donation Form block, plus the shortcodes [donor_merchant], [donor_merchant campaign="N"], [donor_merchant_progress campaign="N"], and [donor_merchant_portal]. A Shortcodes tab in Settings lists each one with your campaign IDs filled in, ready to copy.
  • Six accent colors or a custom color, and three button shapes (pill, rounded, sharp), with a live preview in Settings.
  • Your own wording: switch “donation” and “donate” to “gift” and “give”, or to your own words, everywhere donors see them, and reword any other text with a simple replacement table.

Records that match your processor

Renewals, refunds, and bank payments that settle days later are recorded from Stripe’s and PayPal’s signed webhooks, so the donations list lines up with your gateway account. A partial refund leaves the gift in your totals, and only a full refund marks it refunded.

How it stays secure

Payment details are collected by Stripe and PayPal directly in the donor’s browser. No card number, expiration date, or CVC is ever transmitted to or stored on your server. Donation totals are recomputed on the server, payment status is confirmed server-to-gateway, and webhook signatures are verified.

Card testing and spam are handled without a CAPTCHA by default: a hidden honeypot field, a signed check that rejects forms submitted impossibly fast, per-IP rate limiting, and a server-side minimum amount. If your payment processor asks you to add a CAPTCHA, the donor_merchant_pre_donation filter lets you plug one in without editing the plugin.

What it does not do

Donor Merchant has no peer-to-peer fundraising, text-to-give, matching-gift company lookup, or drag-and-drop form builder. Forms are set up from the Settings screens.

External services

To process donations this plugin connects to third-party payment and (optionally) marketing services. Nothing is sent until you enable and configure a given service.

  • Stripe (only when Stripe is enabled). The Stripe.js library is loaded from https://js.stripe.com on pages that display the donation form, so payment details can be collected securely in the donor’s browser. Your server also calls the Stripe API at https://api.stripe.com to create payment intents, customers, and subscriptions, and to verify payments. Data sent: donation amount and currency, the donor’s name, email and phone number if given, an internal reference for the donation, and the payment details the donor enters (handled by Stripe – they do not touch your server). Stripe terms: https://stripe.com/legal – privacy: https://stripe.com/privacy
  • PayPal (only when PayPal is enabled). The PayPal JS SDK is loaded from https://www.paypal.com on pages with the donation form. Your server calls the PayPal API (https://api-m.paypal.com, or https://api-m.sandbox.paypal.com in sandbox mode) to create and capture orders and subscriptions. Data sent: donation amount, currency, and an internal reference. PayPal terms: https://www.paypal.com/legalhub – privacy: https://www.paypal.com/privacy
  • Mailchimp (optional – only when you enable it). By default the form shows a “keep me updated” checkbox and only opted-in donors are sent. If you switch that checkbox off in the settings, every donor is added to the audience, so leave it on unless you have another basis for contacting them. Your server calls the Mailchimp API (https://<dc>.api.mailchimp.com) to add the donor to the audience you choose. Data sent: donor email and name. Mailchimp terms: https://mailchimp.com/legal/terms/ – privacy: https://mailchimp.com/legal/privacy/
  • Outgoing webhooks (optional). If you enter one or more webhook URLs, completed-donation data is POSTed to those URLs – which you control and choose (e.g. your Zapier or Make endpoint). No third party receives data unless you configure it.

Getting started

  1. Install and activate the plugin.
  2. Go to Donor Merchant → Settings → Payments and paste your Stripe and/or PayPal API keys.
  3. Add the Donation Form block (or [donor_merchant]) to any page.
  4. If you accept recurring gifts, add the webhook URL shown on the Payments tab to your Stripe or PayPal account.
  5. Test with Stripe test mode or the PayPal sandbox, then switch to live.

plugins.name: Advanced Shipping Rate Builder – Table Rate, Conditional & Weight Based Shipping
plugins.author: actpro
plugins.short_description: Table rate shipping for WooCommerce. Conditional, weight based and flat rate shipping rules, a visual builder, cart simulator and free shipping bar.
plugins.description:
Advanced Shipping Rate Builder is a table rate shipping plugin for WooCommerce. It lets you build exactly the rates your store needs — table rate shipping, conditional shipping, weight based shipping, flat rate shipping and free shipping — and see what customers will pay before they do.

Try the live demo — a full WooCommerce store with the plugin installed. No signup, nothing to install.

Set up table rate shipping by cart total, weight or item count. Add conditional shipping rules that only apply to certain products, categories or shipping classes. Charge weight based shipping per kilogram, a flat rate per order, a cost per item, or a percentage of the order. All from one visual rule builder, with no code.

Every rule reads as a sentence: WHERE (which WooCommerce zones) → WHEN (conditions) → THEN (what to charge) → SHOW AS (the label at checkout). A live plain-language summary restates the whole rule as you edit, and the built-in Simulator runs any test cart through the real engine, showing which rules matched, which were skipped and exactly why.

Why merchants choose it

Most shipping plugins make you guess. This one shows you the answer before your customer sees it: a live checkout preview while you edit, and a simulator that runs your real rules against any test cart. “Why didn’t my rule apply?” stops being a support ticket.

Shipping scenarios you can build

  • Free shipping over an amount — free once the cart reaches $50, with a progress bar telling shoppers how much more to add
  • Weight based shipping — $5 up to 5 kg, $9 to 20 kg, $15 above, as a proper weight table
  • Flat rate shipping per order — one price for everything, or one price per item
  • Bulky item shipping — a higher rate whenever the cart contains a shipping class or category you choose
  • Conditional shipping by product — a rate that only appears when a specific product is in the cart
  • Percentage-based shipping — charge shipping as a percentage of the order subtotal
  • Tiered shipping rates — add an amount for every extra 5 kg, 10 items or $100 of subtotal
  • Local pickup or courier choice — offer several rates at once and let the customer choose
  • One rate only — hide the other shipping methods when your rule applies

Build rates from

  • Flat cost, cost per item, cost per weight, or percentage of the cart subtotal
  • Tiered extras — add amounts per quantity, weight or subtotal range (up to 5 tiers)
  • A free-shipping threshold on any rule (“free when the cart total reaches …”)

Target rules by

  • Your existing WooCommerce shipping zones — no duplicate location setup, ever
  • Cart subtotal, cart weight, item quantity
  • Products, product categories, shipping classes

Merchant-friendly by design

  • Goal-first creation — pick what you want (“free shipping over an amount”, “weight-based rate”, …) and get a working rule to adjust
  • Rule simulator — answer “why didn’t my rule apply?” in seconds, not support tickets
  • Free-shipping progress bar on cart and checkout (“Add €12.50 more for free shipping”), classic and block carts alike
  • Clear resolution: show all matching rates (customer picks) or highest-priority only — stated in plain words on the dashboard
  • Rules never break checkout: a misconfigured rule is skipped and flagged in the dashboard, never fatal

Lightweight & modern

  • Rules live in one indexed table — no post-meta bloat, one query per checkout calculation
  • Zero frontend assets unless the progress bar is shown
  • HPOS compatible, works with classic and Block cart/checkout
  • REST API and WP-CLI (wp wpactpro-sr rules …) included

Free vs Pro

Everything in the free plugin, with no limits on how many rules you create:

  • Cost types: flat rate, per item, per weight, percentage of subtotal
  • Tiered rates by quantity, weight or subtotal — up to 5 tiers per rule
  • Free-shipping threshold on any rule, and the free-shipping progress bar
  • Conditions: cart subtotal, cart weight, item quantity, cart contains product, cart contains category, cart contains shipping class
  • Targeting by your existing WooCommerce shipping zones
  • The visual rule builder, the plain-language rule summary and the live checkout preview
  • The Simulator, showing which rules matched a test cart and why the rest did not
  • Hide other shipping methods, rule priority and resolution modes
  • REST API, WP-CLI, HPOS and Block cart/checkout support

Advanced Shipping Rate Builder Pro adds eleven more conditions and five workflow features:

  • Destination postcode and destination city — charge differently inside a single zone, so “£5 to mainland UK, £15 to the Highlands” no longer needs a second shipping zone. Same wildcard (CB2*) and range (90210...99000) syntax as WooCommerce zones.
  • Dimensional weight, cart volume and longest side in cart — price bulky-but-light parcels the way couriers actually bill them.
  • Customer role — wholesale and B2B shipping rates.
  • Specific customer — one named account’s own negotiated rate.
  • Date range, day of week and time of day — seasonal, holiday and cut-off-time rates.
  • Coupon applied — a shipping rate that responds to a promotion.
  • OR condition groups — one rule that matches several different carts.
  • Shipping decisions log — open any order and see which rule set the rate, and why every other rule did not apply. Answers “why was I charged this?” without reproducing the cart.
  • Shadow mode — run a price change against real traffic, recorded but charging nobody, before it reaches a customer.
  • Surcharge rules — add a handling fee on top of every rate instead of competing with them as another option.
  • Rule warnings — told when a rule can never apply because another always wins first, or when it targets a shipping zone that has been deleted.

Every rule you build in the free version keeps working if a licence lapses — you can still edit, simplify and delete them.

plugins.name: IPA – Indian Pincode Autofill
plugins.author: Mizbahuddin Qasim
plugins.short_description: Fast, automatic Indian PIN code detector and location autofill for WooCommerce checkout with transient caching and full HPOS support.
plugins.description:
IPA – Indian Pincode Autofill streamlines the WooCommerce checkout process for Indian e-commerce stores. When a customer enters a valid 6-digit Indian PIN code at checkout, the plugin instantly detects the corresponding city and state, and autofills the respective fields without disrupting the customer’s typing focus.

By reducing checkout friction and eliminating typos in city and state names, this plugin significantly increases checkout conversion rates and prevents delivery failures caused by mismatched address details.

Why Choose IPA?

  • Lightning-Fast Autofill: Detects location within milliseconds as soon as 6 digits are typed.
  • Intelligent Debouncing (500ms): Eliminates duplicate requests while typing.
  • High-Performance Transients Caching: Caches verified PIN codes in WordPress Transients for 30 days to ensure instantaneous lookup and minimal API load.
  • Country-Specific Checkout Ordering: Intelligently reorders checkout fields for India (PIN Code -> City -> District -> State) using WooCommerce’s native locale filter, leaving all other countries 100% untouched.
  • Dedicated District Field Support: Optionally display a dedicated District checkout field with toggleable autofill and customer edit/lock controls.
  • Configurable City Value Source: Choose between “District as City” (courier & logistics standard) or “Smart Town Mode” (filters out bazaar and neighborhood street names).
  • Zero Impact on International Orders: The plugin operates strictly when the selected country is India (IN). For US, UK, EU, or any non-Indian checkout, the plugin remains completely inactive.
  • Seamless Compatibility: Works with standard WooCommerce checkout, WooCommerce Gutenberg Blocks, AJAX fragments refresh, One Page Checkout plugins, and modern themes.
  • Dedicated Admin Settings: Separate admin menu with toggle switches for enabling/disabling the plugin, toggling city, district, and state autofill, locking fields as readonly, or reordering checkout fields.
  • Live PIN Code Tester: Test any PIN code directly in the WordPress admin to inspect live API results, cached responses, and state codes.
  • 100% HPOS Ready: Fully compatible with WooCommerce High-Performance Order Storage (HPOS).
  • Accessible & Secure: Built using WordPress Coding Standards (WPCS), strict nonces, input sanitization, and output escaping.

External services

This plugin relies on a 3rd-party external API service to verify and resolve Indian PIN codes into geographical locations:

  • Service Name: Postal Pincode API
  • Provider URL: https://api.postalpincode.in/
  • Service Purpose: Resolves a 6-digit Indian postal code (PIN) into its respective District (City) and State name.
  • Data Transmitted: Only the 6-digit numeric PIN code entered by the user (e.g. 302001). No personal information, names, email addresses, street addresses, phone numbers, or IP addresses are ever transmitted or stored remotely.
  • When Data is Transmitted: An outbound HTTPS GET request is made exclusively when a customer enters exactly 6 digits into the billing or shipping postcode field and the selected country is India (IN).
  • Terms of Service: https://api.postalpincode.in/
  • Privacy Policy: https://api.postalpincode.in/

plugins.name: SendToMP
plugins.author: Mike Rouse
plugins.short_description: Let your visitors send verified messages to their MP or a Peer, with double opt-in confirmation and lookup against the UK Parliament Members API.
plugins.description:
SendToMP lets your website visitors send verified messages directly to their Member of Parliament or a member of the House of Lords. Every message goes through a double opt-in confirmation flow, so only genuine constituents can contact their representatives.

Built by a former parliamentary assistant who understands how MP offices process inbound correspondence, SendToMP is designed to produce messages that get read and acted upon.

Every feature is available to everyone. There is no paid tier, no licence key, no message quota, and nothing is held back.

How it works:

  1. A visitor fills in your form with their name, email address, postcode, and message.
  2. SendToMP looks up their MP from the postcode, or lets them search for a Peer by name.
  3. A confirmation email is sent to the visitor to verify their identity.
  4. The visitor clicks through and confirms on your site. Only then is the message sent.
  5. The MP or Peer receives a properly formatted email and can reply to the constituent directly.

Form plugin support:

  • Gravity Forms
  • WPForms
  • Contact Form 7
  • A webhook / REST API endpoint for custom integrations

Key features:

  • Double opt-in confirmation, so a message is only ever sent by the person whose inbox it came from
  • Postcode-based MP lookup against the UK Parliament Members API
  • House of Lords member search and selection
  • Configurable email templates with merge tags
  • Submission logging with delivery status tracking
  • Rate limiting and anti-spam protection, per email address, per IP, and per postcode
  • Address overrides, for when a member’s published address is wrong or missing
  • Email delivery through your existing SMTP plugin, your own SMTP server, or Brevo
  • A copy-and-paste privacy notice describing exactly what the plugin stores and sends

A note on data. The constituent’s postcode is sent to the UK Parliament Members API in order to identify their representative. Nothing else leaves your site for that lookup: not their name, not their email address, and not their message. If you configure Brevo as your email provider, the message is sent to Brevo for delivery. See the External services section below for the detail.

External services

This plugin relies on one external service to function, and optionally on a second if you choose it as your email provider.

1. UK Parliament Members API (required)

The plugin uses the UK Parliament Members API to work out which MP or Peer represents a constituent, and to obtain the contact address that Parliament publishes for that member. The plugin cannot do this locally: the mapping from postcode to constituency to sitting member changes with boundary reviews, by-elections and appointments, and only Parliament publishes it. No account or API key is required, and the plugin sends no credentials.

Data sent, and when it is sent:

  • When a visitor uses the “Find my MP” preview on your form, their postcode is sent, so the matched MP can be shown before they submit.
  • When a visitor submits the form, their postcode is sent, to resolve the member the message will go to.
  • When an administrator searches for a member by name in the plugin’s admin screens, the search text is sent.
  • Once a member has been identified, the plugin requests that member’s public profile and published contact details using their Parliament member ID.

The constituent’s name, email address, and message content are never sent to Parliament. Responses are cached in your site’s transients so the same postcode is not looked up repeatedly.

Service: UK Parliament Members API, https://members-api.parliament.uk/
Terms of use (Open Parliament Licence): https://www.parliament.uk/site-information/copyright-parliament/open-parliament-licence/
Privacy policy: https://www.parliament.uk/site-information/data-protection/

2. Brevo (optional)

Brevo is one of the email delivery providers you may choose on the Email Delivery tab. It is only contacted if you select it and enter your own Brevo API key. If you use your existing SMTP plugin, your own SMTP server, or the WordPress default mailer instead, the plugin never contacts Brevo.

Data sent, and when it is sent: when Brevo is the selected provider, each outgoing email is sent to Brevo’s transactional email API at the moment it is delivered. That includes the recipient’s address, the constituent’s name and email address as the reply-to, the subject, and the message body. This applies both to the confirmation email sent to the constituent and to the message delivered to the MP or Peer.

Service: Brevo, https://www.brevo.com/
Terms of use: https://www.brevo.com/legal/termsofuse/
Privacy policy: https://www.brevo.com/legal/privacypolicy/

The plugin contacts no other external service. It sends no analytics, usage data, or telemetry anywhere.

plugins.name: Vanquish Shipping Tracking – Order Tracking & Carrier Links for WooCommerce
plugins.author: Vanquish
plugins.short_description: Tracking numbers on WooCommerce orders and emails: 1,600+ carriers with logos, a direct tracking link and a Track button. No account needed.
plugins.description:
Every parcel you ship brings the same question: where is my order? Vanquish Shipping Tracking for WooCommerce answers it before it is asked. Add a carrier and a tracking number to an order, and your customer finds them in the order emails and on their order page — with the carrier’s logo and a link to the carrier’s tracking page, the tracking number already filled in whenever the carrier supports it.

HPOS compatible · 1,600+ carriers, with logos · Works with ShipStation · Shipment Tracking API compatible · No account, no API key, no data sent · WPML & Polylang ready

How it works

  1. Install and activate the plugin. WooCommerce is the only requirement.
  2. Under Shipping Tracking → Shipping companies, switch on the carriers you ship with. You can skip this: until you choose, every carrier is offered.
  3. Open an order, pick the carrier, type the tracking number and press Update — or let ShipStation or your shipping service send it: it lands on the order by itself.
  4. Your customer gets the tracking — with a link straight to the carrier — in the order emails and on their order page.

Switching from WooCommerce Shipment Tracking?

Your tools keep working: shipping services, label printers and ERPs that send tracking to WooCommerce Shipment Tracking find the same API here, and ShipStation is supported out of the box. The tracking already on your orders comes across by itself, and the extension’s own data is left where it is — so trying this plugin costs you nothing.

Free, with no strings attached

Everything in the free version works without an account, an API key or a subscription, and sends no data anywhere: custom carriers, logos, the message editor and the customer tracking form included.

Premium: your customers follow the parcel without leaving your store

The free version sends your customer to the carrier’s website. Premium brings the whole journey onto your own order page:

  • Live shipment status — picked up, in transit, out for delivery, delivered — shown as a timeline drawn by your store, in your theme, not a widget embedded from someone else’s site.
  • Emails at the moments that matter — “out for delivery”, “available for pickup”, “delivered”, sent as real WooCommerce emails — and an alert for you when a parcel reports a problem or stops moving.
  • Every parcel of an order, each with its own link and its own timeline.

It runs on your own AfterShip, TrackingMore or track123 account: you bring the API key, requests go straight from your store to the service.

No account with a tracking service? The 17TRACK widget shows the steps of the parcel on the same page with nothing to set up, in 17TRACK’s own box.

Free features

Carriers

  • 1,600+ predefined carriers worldwide, most of them with their logo, each linking to its own tracking page. For about 400 of them the link opens the parcel directly, with the tracking number already filled in.
  • A universal tracking page for the others — optionally, the carriers that have no direct link (or all of them) open Track123 or 17TRACK with the tracking number already filled in. These are free pages of other companies, with their own brand and ads.
  • Only the carriers you use — pick them from a searchable grid showing each carrier’s logo, country and a “Direct link” mark, so the order screen offers three carriers instead of 1,600.
  • A default carrier, optionally, preselected on orders that have no tracking yet.
  • Your own carriers — a local courier, your own deliveries — with a tracking URL template that takes the tracking code, the postcode and the country.

What your customers see

  • The tracking in the standard WooCommerce order emails and on the order details / My Account page: the carrier’s logo and name, the tracking number and link, and a “Track shipment” button in your email colours.
  • Guest customers too: the tracking also appears on the order confirmation page, which needs no login, and the [vanstr_tracking_form] shortcode lets anyone look up an order with its number and billing email. Failed attempts are rate limited.
  • You decide where and when: which order statuses show the tracking, whether it goes into the emails, and whether it sits before or after the order table — separately for the emails and the order page.

Messages

  • Two fully editable messages, one for the order page and one for the emails, with a visual editor and a live preview beside it, in your WooCommerce email colours, with one parcel or two, at desktop or phone width.
  • Placeholders you insert with a click: the carrier’s logo and name, the tracking number and link, the “Track shipment” button, the order number ([order_id]), the order page and the dispatch date.
  • Three ready-made messages to start from: one click fills the editor, and from there the text is yours to change.
  • A box of its own in the emails: the tracking sits in a bordered block, set apart from the order details around it.
  • Multilingual ready: with WPML or Polylang active, every customer-facing message can be entered in each language, one tab per language.

Built for the way a shop ships

  • Carrier, tracking number and dispatch date in the Shipping tracking box, in the side column of the order screen, with a “Track this shipment” link to check the parcel.
  • The dispatch date can start on today’s date, for shops that enter the tracking on the day they ship.
  • Mark the order as completed with one switch, at the bottom of the same box, on orders that are not completed yet.
  • An order note every time the tracking is added or changed, timestamped by WooCommerce — a record of when each parcel was booked, kept where your customers never see it.
  • A tracking column in the admin orders list: the status, carrier, tracking link and dispatch date of each shipment in one compact box, with each shipment marked Shipped or Not shipped — no extra order statuses to clutter your reports.

Works with your shipping tools

  • A REST API compatible with WooCommerce Shipment Tracking — shipping services, label tools and ERPs built to send tracking to the official WooCommerce Shipment Tracking extension send it to this plugin just the same, with nothing to set up. Active whenever neither that extension nor Advanced Shipment Tracking is installed.
  • ShipStation — the tracking ShipStation for WooCommerce reports when it ships an order is added automatically, and ShipStation’s own tracking note is kept private, so your customer is not told twice.
  • One tracking per order in the free version — when a service sends a second one for the same order, it is kept on the order, never lost, and you are told: on the order itself, in the admin, and in a summary email at most once a day, which you can turn off.

For developers and for switching plugins

  • vanstr_set_tracking(), a documented function for attaching tracking from your own code when your warehouse software or carrier plugin books the parcel.
  • Automatic migration of your settings and each order’s tracking from the legacy “WooCommerce Shipping Tracking” (CodeCanyon) plugin.

Premium features

  • In-site shipping timeline — show the live shipment status (picked up, in transit, out for delivery, delivered…) as a timeline on the order page, drawn by your own site rather than embedded from the provider. Bring your own API key from AfterShip, TrackingMore or track123; requests go straight from your site to the service you chose. Includes a one-click connection test.
  • Tracking without an account — as an alternative to the timeline, the 17TRACK widget shows the steps of each parcel on the order page with no account and no API key. It is 17TRACK’s own widget, with its logo and an advertising banner that cannot be removed, and it does not feed the status emails, the alerts or the orders list.
  • Multiple shipments per order — added with + Add shipment, each parcel with its own carrier, tracking number, dispatch date, note and the products it contains. Every further tracking a shipping service or ShipStation sends becomes one, and those the free version kept appear by themselves. On the order screen each parcel folds into a row you open with a click, and the box tells you when a product is in no parcel.
  • Works with Vanquish Multiple Addresses Premium — an order it splits by destination opens here with one shipment per destination and its products already assigned: you only type the tracking numbers.
  • PayPal tracking — with WooCommerce PayPal Payments, the tracking of each order paid through it is added to the PayPal transaction, whether you type it in, import it or a shipping service sends it. PayPal takes the tracking into account when releasing held payments and settling “item not received” disputes.
  • Per-product tracking — when a shipment is tied to specific products, its tracking link is shown next to those products on the order page and in the emails (can be turned off).
  • Shipping estimates for products — show an estimated shipping (dispatch) date on the product page, cart, checkout, order and emails, computed from rules you set per product, category or tag (shipping days, cut-off hour, processing days, holidays, optional date range), with a configurable out-of-stock text. The [vanstr_estimated_date] shortcode places it anywhere, with product_id to choose the product.
  • Delivery estimates for shipping methods — attach a “3–5 days” style estimate to each shipping method, shown with the method in the cart and at checkout. Works in both the block and the classic checkout.
  • Requested delivery date — let customers pick a preferred delivery date (and an optional merchant-defined time slot) at checkout, within the window you configure. Works in both the block and the classic checkout; editable from the admin order screen.
  • CSV import — drag and drop a CSV of tracking codes (one row per shipment, separator detected on its own) and say how its dates are written, so 07/09 is never read the wrong way round. An optional scheduled import fetches a CSV from a URL you configure.
  • Quick assign — fill in tracking for many orders from a single screen: set the carrier, the date and the customer email once for the whole batch, scan or type each number and press Enter for the next row, and see on every row whether it is ready, incomplete or untouched before you save. With filters and an optional status change after saving.
  • “Order shipped” notification email — a real WooCommerce email, configured under WooCommerce → Settings → Emails like any other.
  • Automatic shipment monitoring — check your tracked shipments on a schedule: tell customers when their parcel is out for delivery, available for pickup or delivered, and be alerted yourself when one reports a problem or stops moving for a number of days you choose. Each event is announced once per shipment. What the carrier reports also shows in the orders list (in transit, out for delivery, delivered, exception), with each order summed up as shipped, partially shipped or delivered.

Screenshots, plans and answers on the plugin’s page: vanquishplugins.com/plugins/shipping-tracking.

Carrier names and logos are trademarks of their respective owners, shown only to identify each carrier. The logos ship with the plugin: displaying them never contacts any external server.

External services

The free version does not send any data to external services. It only builds links, which the customer opens in their own browser: by default, links to the carriers’ own tracking pages.

If you choose so under Shipping Tracking → Settings → Tracking link (off by default), those links open a universal tracking page instead, with the tracking number in the address. Your site still sends nothing: the customer opens the page by clicking the link. These are free services of other companies, subject to their own terms:

  • Track123 — https://www.track123.com/ (terms, privacy)
  • 17TRACK — https://www.17track.net/ (privacy, copyright notice)

The premium version can connect to external services. All of them are configured and controlled entirely by you:

  1. Tracking providers (in-site timeline). When you enable the shipping timeline and select a provider, the plugin sends the order’s tracking number and carrier code to that provider’s API to retrieve the shipment status, using your own account’s API key. No data is sent until you enter an API key and select the provider. Supported providers:
    • AfterShip — https://www.aftership.com/ (terms, privacy)
    • TrackingMore, operated by CWILL — https://www.trackingmore.com/ (terms, privacy)
    • track123 — https://www.track123.com/ (terms, privacy)
  2. 17TRACK widget. If you choose the 17TRACK widget instead of a provider, the order page and the tracking form load 17TRACK’s script in your customer’s browser, which shows each parcel in a frame served by 17TRACK. The browser sends 17TRACK the tracking number, the address of your site and, as with any embedded content, its IP address. Nothing is loaded until you select the widget. 17TRACK’s privacy policy is linked above.
  3. Scheduled CSV import. If you enable the scheduled bulk import, the plugin periodically downloads a CSV file from the URL that you configure (typically a feed published by your own warehouse or fulfilment service). No data is sent to that URL; the file is only fetched.
  4. PayPal. When WooCommerce PayPal Payments is active, the tracking number and carrier name of each order paid through it are passed to that plugin, which adds them to the order’s PayPal transaction with your own PayPal account. Nothing is sent for orders paid any other way. PayPal — https://www.paypal.com/ (terms, privacy)

More WooCommerce plugins by Vanquish

  • Vanquish Upload Files for WooCommerce – let customers upload files (even large ones) on the product, cart, checkout and order pages, for custom, personalized and print-on-demand products.
  • Vanquish Multiple Addresses for WooCommerce – give customers an address book: save multiple billing and shipping addresses and pick one at checkout.
  • Vanquish Attach Me – Order & Product Attachments for WooCommerce – attach files to orders and products, show them to the customer and send them with the order emails.

plugins.name: H6 Smart Shipping & Payment Control for WooCommerce
plugins.author: Jo Cox
plugins.short_description: Hide, limit, rename or charge for WooCommerce delivery options and payment methods, with simple rules based on the order and customer.
plugins.description:
H6 Smart Shipping & Payment Control lets you decide which delivery options and payment methods each customer sees at checkout, and what they cost, without writing code. Hide cash on delivery outside the UK, offer free delivery only over £50, let trade customers pay by bank transfer, or add a charge for remote postcodes.

It is built for shop owners, not developers. Every rule is written out in one plain sentence, such as “When the delivery country is not United Kingdom → hide Cash on delivery”, and a “Try it out” tab shows what would happen to an order before your customers see it.

It works alongside your normal WooCommerce shipping zones and payment settings, and never replaces them.

Everything is included. There is no paid version and nothing is locked.

Good for:

  • Offering free delivery, collection or couriers only when it makes sense
  • Stopping cash on delivery, or any other payment method, where you do not want it
  • Letting trade and wholesale customers pay on account or by bank transfer
  • Charging for remote postcodes, heavy parcels, small orders or card payments
  • Changing delivery options at weekends, on bank holidays or after a cut-off time

Decide when a rule applies

Build each rule from one or more conditions, and choose whether all of them or any of them must be true.

  • The cart: subtotal, weight, number of items, products, categories, shipping classes and coupons
  • The address: delivery country, postcode (with wildcards such as IV* and ranges such as PA20…PA80), county or state, and shipping zone
  • The customer: guests, anyone logged in, or customer types such as trade customers
  • The time: days of the week, times of day and date ranges, in your shop’s time zone
  • A rule with no conditions applies to every order

Change delivery options

  • Hide delivery options, such as free delivery for very heavy orders
  • Only offer certain delivery options and hide the rest
  • Rename a delivery option, such as “Flat rate” to “Next-day courier”
  • Change the delivery cost: add an amount or a percentage, take some off, or set a new price
  • Choose an option for every zone, or for one zone only

Change payment methods

  • Hide payment methods, such as cash on delivery outside the UK
  • Only offer certain payment methods, such as bank transfer for trade customers
  • Rename a payment method for matching orders

Add charges

  • A set charge, such as a small-order or handling charge
  • A percentage of the subtotal, such as a remote-area surcharge
  • An amount for every item in the cart
  • A charge for choosing a particular payment method, such as cash on delivery, which appears in the total as soon as the customer chooses it
  • Optional minimum and maximum charges, your own name for the charge, and tax if you need it

Tell customers what changed

Add an optional message to any rule, such as “Cash on delivery is only available in the UK”. It is shown on the basket and checkout while the rule applies, and updates as the customer changes their address or payment method.

Try it out

Describe an order (what is in the cart, where it is going, who is buying and how they are paying) and see which rules would apply, why, and what they would do, including the charge worked out for that order.

Easy to manage

  • A plain-English summary of your rules at the top of the screen
  • Tabs for delivery, payment and charges
  • Switch any rule on or off, and drag rules into the order they should run
  • Rules with an unfinished condition are clearly marked so nothing fails silently
  • One switch pauses every rule without deleting them

plugins.description:
We have created this plugin to make it easy for our affiliates to generate quality moving leads. At the same time we wanted to provide the best conversion rate possible for our affiliate partners. This is why we’ve spent a lot of time creating the additional features of this plugin.

Please note that this plugin requires a free API key for the MoveAdvisor lead system in order to capture leads.

How does the plugin work
Visitors visit a website where they see the form that is generated by the plugin. If a visitor is about to move, he or she will enter their move details and contact information and will submit the form. Based on the move information from the lead they may get one of the following:

  • The user’s lead will be sent to MoveAdvisor and is sent to moving companies that will contact the user with more information regarding their move. The user will see a “Thank You” message that the lead is submitted and that he or she should expect their moving quote soon.

  • For some US, Canadian and UK leads, the MoveAdvisor system may decide to call the user directly and connect the user with the moving company operator in real time. In those cases instead of a “Thank You” page, users will see “Wait, we are calling you now” page. Then the MoveAdvisor bot with Artificial Intelligence will call the user and will connect the user with a moving expert over the phone. The call is also considered a lead. Please note that this feature is still in beta.

Currently this form consists of 4 different forms that are automatically displayed to the customer based on the location. You do not need to select which form is displayed to who as the plugin does that automatically. Here are the different form types:

  • US Moving leads form
    For users that are moving within The US. The form is in Imperial units and is tailored to the default preferences of the US users. Users will be able to switch to international form if they are moving out of the USA.

  • Canadian Moving leads form
    For users that are moving within Canada. The form is in Metric units and is tailored to the default preferences of the Canadian users. Users will be able to switch to international form if they are moving out of Canada.

  • Australian Moving leads form
    For users that are moving within Australia. The form is in Metric units and is tailored to the default preferences of the users in Australia. Users will be able to switch to international form if they are moving out of Australia.

  • German Moving leads form
    For users that are moving within Germany. The form is in Metric units and is tailored to the default preferences of the users in Germany. Users will be able to switch to international form if they are moving out of Germany.

  • UK Moving leads form
    For users that are moving within The UK. The form is in Metric units and is tailored to the default preferences of the users in The United Kingdom. Users will be able to switch to international form if they are moving out of the UK.

  • International Moving leads form
    This form is for users that are moving between countries.

Clear cover options and direct customer servicing through your store, subject to eligibility, policy terms, conditions, and exclusions.

Key features

  • Automatic policy creation on order processing/completion
  • Admin screens for settings, API logs, and issued policies
  • WooCommerce High-Performance Order Storage (HPOS) compatible

This plugin requires an active WooCommerce installation and MarchGuard store credentials (Store ID and Store PIN) obtained from TH March.

March Guard and the MarchGuard service are owned and operated by T.H. March & Co. Limited. The plugin was developed for TH March by Webcomp Digitex (https://webcompdigitex.com).

External services

This plugin connects to the MarchGuard insurance service, operated by T.H. March & Co. Limited, to provide insurance quotes and to create insurance policies. This connection is essential to the plugin’s core function — without it, insurance quotes cannot be retrieved and policies cannot be issued.

What the service is used for and when data is sent:

  • Requesting a quote — when a customer views an eligible product, cart, or checkout, the plugin requests a premium quote. The following data is sent: item description, item value, product category, insurance term, and (for rating) a postcode placeholder.
  • Finalising a quote / creating a policy — when an order containing insurance is processed, the plugin submits the customer’s details to issue a policy. The following data is sent: customer title, first and last name, billing address, postcode, country, email address, and the order/invoice number, together with the insured item details.
  • Retrieving policy certificates — the plugin requests the policy certificate (PDF) for an issued policy using the policy reference number.

Requests are sent to the following endpoints:

  • Staging: https://stage.marchguard.com/public_services
  • Production: https://www.marchguard.com/public_services

The endpoint used depends on the “Environment” setting you select in the plugin settings.

Service provider, terms, and privacy:

  • Service provider: T.H. March & Co. Limited (authorised and regulated by the Financial Conduct Authority, FCA Register number 304812).
  • Terms of Service: https://www.thmarch.co.uk/March-Guard-IPID.pdf (March Guard Insurance Product Information Document — the terms, cover and exclusions of the product this plugin sells)
  • Privacy Policy: https://www.thmarch.co.uk/March-Guard-Full-Wording.pdf (March Guard full policy wording; the “Data Protection” section sets out how customer information is used)

Both documents are specific to the March Guard scheme and are the same ones the plugin shows to customers before they consent to cover.

By using this plugin and enabling insurance, you agree that customer data required to provide a quote and issue a policy will be transmitted to the MarchGuard service as described above. You are responsible for disclosing this data sharing in your own store’s privacy policy.

Privacy

This plugin stores the following data in your WordPress database:

  • API logs ({prefix}_thmarch_api_logs) — records of requests to and responses from the MarchGuard service, used for troubleshooting. These may contain customer details submitted during policy creation.
  • Policies ({prefix}_thmarch_policies) — issued policy records including policy number, customer email and name, item value, premium, and coverage amount.

Insurance selections are also temporarily held in the WooCommerce customer session during checkout and stored in order meta once an order is placed.

plugins.name: ModuleFest Pet Groomer – Pet Grooming Business Manager
plugins.author: modulefest
plugins.short_description: Bookings, clients, pets and invoicing for dog and cat groomers, with a staff app and a customer portal.
plugins.description:
Built for grooming salons and mobile groomers.

The question a groomer answers more than any other is how long a dog will take and what to charge for it. The honest answer depends on the coat, not the weight: two cockapoos of the same size can be an hour apart if one is silk-coated and the other is matted wool. ModuleFest Pet Groomer includes a coat and clip library that prices and times every groom from the dog’s coat, with eight coat types ready to use, a per-coat time multiplier and surcharge, and breed-to-coat suggestions. Also included: a body map for warts and sensitive spots, before-and-after photo galleries and vaccination tracking.

It is a complete booking and client system for a grooming business: bookings, clients, pets, invoicing and payments in one WordPress install the business owns outright, behind an installable, mobile-first staff app and a self-service customer portal.

It shows only the fields a groomer actually needs — coat types, breed pricing, a body map and before-and-after galleries — rather than a general-purpose system you have to prune.

What you get

  • Bookings and calendar — drag-and-drop diary, recurring visits, availability rules and a booking editor that fits on a phone
  • Clients and pets — full history, per-pet care profiles, vaccination compliance and an interactive body map
  • Invoicing and payments — deposits, scheduled auto-invoicing, statements you send or print, PDF and print output, and card payments through Stripe if you want them
  • Customer portal — clients book, cancel, reschedule and pay themselves, without emailing you
  • Installable app — works on any phone with no app store: the day’s dogs in order, photos and report cards, and it keeps working when the signal does not
  • Import and export — bring your existing clients in with a guided wizard; take everything with you whenever you like
  • Your branding — branded login and booking pages with QR codes
  • Demo data you can load and remove, so you can see the system working before you use it

Everything here is free

Everything this plugin contains is free to use in full, for as long as you like. There is no
trial, no licence key, no quota and nothing that stops working after a while.

A separate paid plugin, ModuleFest Pet Groomer Pro, is available from our website for businesses that want
more: reminders and newsletters, statements that send themselves, packages and sale prices, finance reports and a report builder,
mileage, accounting integrations, team members with rotas and commission, a round planner,
customer segments, waiting lists, loyalty cards, automations and website designs. You
never need it to run your business on this plugin, and this plugin never downloads or installs
anything.

More from ModuleFest

We make free WordPress plugins for small businesses. Others on WordPress.org:

  • ModuleFest Pet Walker — for dog walkers

All of them are on our WordPress.org profile, and there is more about us at modulefest.com.

Privacy and external services

ModuleFest Pet Groomer keeps your data on your own site. It does not contact us or anybody else
on its own — no analytics, no telemetry, no licence check and nothing on a schedule.

Some features need an outside service to work. Every one is listed here, with what gets sent and
when. Anything marked only if you turn it on needs you to enter your own details or tick a
setting first, and sends nothing until you do.

Maps — OpenStreetMap, only if you turn it on. Settings → General → Maps and postcode lookup is off until you switch it on. With it on, when you open a route map (for mobile grooming), your browser loads map
tiles from tile.openstreetmap.org, and the plugin fetches tiles server-side when it draws a
static map into a report. What is sent: the map area being viewed. No client or pet details are
ever included.
Terms: https://operations.osmfoundation.org/policies/tiles/ · Privacy:
https://osmfoundation.org/wiki/Privacy_Policy

Postcode and address lookup — Postcodes.io (UK) and OpenStreetMap Nominatim (elsewhere), only if you turn it on.
With the same setting on, when a booking or client needs placing on a map or measuring for mileage, the client’s postcode
is looked up to get approximate coordinates. In the UK it is sent to api.postcodes.io. For a
business in another country (Settings → General → Country) it is sent to
nominatim.openstreetmap.org instead, or, where a client has no postcode, their address line.
Requests to Nominatim identify your site’s address, as their usage policy asks. No name, phone,
email or pet detail is ever sent. Results are cached, so a place is only looked up once.
Terms and privacy: https://postcodes.io/ · https://operations.osmfoundation.org/policies/nominatim/ ·
https://osmfoundation.org/wiki/Privacy_Policy

App notifications — web push. If you or a member of staff allow notifications in the staff
app, new-booking alerts are delivered through the push service of that person’s own browser
(Google for Chrome, Mozilla for Firefox, Apple for Safari). What is sent: a short notice that
something needs attention, encrypted so the push service cannot read it. Nothing is sent to
anyone who has not allowed notifications.
Terms and privacy: https://policies.google.com/privacy · https://www.mozilla.org/en-US/privacy/firefox/ ·
https://www.apple.com/legal/privacy/

ModuleFest newsletter sign-up — support.modulefest.com, only when you press Subscribe. The About screen has a Get updates card. Only when you tick its consent box and press Subscribe, the plugin sends your name, your email, this site’s address and the plugin’s name and version to ModuleFest, so we can send you the Pet Groomer newsletter you asked for. Nothing is sent on activation, on a schedule or in the background, and the email address is not kept on your site. No feature depends on subscribing.
Privacy: https://modulefest.com/privacy/ · Terms: https://modulefest.com/terms/

The following are all only if you turn them on:

  • Stripe — card payments and deposits. Sends invoice amounts and the customer’s email to Stripe when you take a payment. https://stripe.com/gb/legal/consumer · https://stripe.com/gb/privacy
  • Twilio — text messages to your customers. Sends the recipient’s mobile number and the message. https://www.twilio.com/en-us/legal/tos · https://www.twilio.com/en-us/legal/privacy

plugins.name: Netro Ads – Pixel & Conversions API for Meta, Google Ads and ChatGPT
plugins.author: netrobit
plugins.short_description: Measure phone, WhatsApp and form conversions. Meta Pixel, Conversions API, Google Ads, GA4 and ChatGPT Ads from one screen, without code.
plugins.description:
On a service business site the conversion is a phone call, a WhatsApp message or a form — not a checkout. Most measurement setups never record those, and nothing on the screen says so: the pixel loads, the campaign runs, and the conversion column stays empty.

Netro Ads measures them. Paste your IDs into one screen and phone clicks, WhatsApp clicks and form submissions are reported to Meta, Google Ads, GA4, Tag Manager and ChatGPT Ads — no code in your theme, no tag manager to learn, nothing to mark up on each page. WooCommerce purchases are included when you have a shop.

It installs the Meta Pixel, the Meta Conversions API, Google Ads conversion tracking, Google Analytics 4, Google Tag Manager and the ChatGPT Ads (OpenAI) Measurement Pixel and Conversions API.

It is server-side tracking without a tag server: every conversion is sent from the browser and from your WordPress server (Meta CAPI and OpenAI Conversions API), so an ad blocker or an event name Meta restricts in the browser does not cost you the conversion. Call tracking and WhatsApp click tracking work on any theme, and the consent gate (GDPR, Google Consent Mode v2) is on by default.

The browser event and the server event share a single event ID, so each platform de-duplicates them and counts one conversion instead of two. One user action gets one ID, used for every platform.

Google Ads, Google Analytics 4 and Google Tag Manager

Paste a GA4 measurement ID (G-…), a Tag Manager container (GTM-…) and a Google Ads conversion ID (AW-…) — or the whole snippet Google gives you; the IDs are read out of it. The same actions are then reported to Google:

  • Google Ads conversions for form submissions, phone clicks, WhatsApp clicks and other contact links (email, Messenger, Telegram), each with its own conversion label or one shared contact label. A missing label is reported in the status list: Google ignores a conversion without one and shows no error.
  • GA4 events: page_view, generate_lead, contact (with the method: phone, WhatsApp, email…) and, with WooCommerce, purchase with value, currency and transaction ID.
  • With WooCommerce, purchases go to Google Ads under their own conversion label, with value, currency and the order number as transaction_id.
  • Tag Manager dataLayer events you can trigger your own tags on: netroads_contact, netroads_lead, netroads_purchase.
  • Google Consent Mode v2 defaults are set before any Google tag loads and updated when the visitor decides.

Google events are sent from the browser; the server-side channel covers Meta and OpenAI.

ChatGPT Ads (OpenAI)

Paste the Pixel ID and a Conversions API key from ChatGPT Ads Manager and the same actions are measured there too: page views, contact clicks and form submissions (lead_created by default), and with WooCommerce contents_viewed, items_added, checkout_started and order_created. OpenAI’s own rules are applied, which differ from Meta’s: names are normalised without spaces before hashing, amounts are sent as integers in the currency’s minor unit (three decimals for KWD, none for JPY), and the oppref click identifier is carried from the landing page to later server events.

What it measures without any setup per page

  • PageView on every page.
  • Contact on every phone, WhatsApp, Messenger, Telegram, SMS or email link — in any theme or page builder, including links added later or inserted by a page builder. One delegated listener covers the whole site; you never mark a link.
  • Lead after a form submission actually succeeds: Contact Form 7, WPForms, Gravity Forms, Elementor Pro Forms, Fluent Forms. A failed or invalid submission produces nothing.
  • ViewContent on the post types you choose.
  • AddToCart, InitiateCheckout and Purchase when WooCommerce is active. Purchase is sent once per order even if the thank-you page is refreshed.
  • Anything else: add data-netroads-conversion="lead" (or "contact") to a button or form.

Built for the things that fail silently

Every failure mode of pixel measurement is silent — nothing errors, conversions just stop arriving. The status panel on the settings screen names each one:

  • Meta restricts certain event names on individual pixels (common on health and aesthetics accounts). The browser drops such an event with no error at all. The plugin reads your pixel’s own configuration, tells you when your contact event is restricted, and lets you pick another name — used on both channels so de-duplication still works.
  • The event ID is generated in the browser, never printed into HTML, so a full page cache cannot hand one ID to every visitor.
  • fbclid is captured on the landing page and carried through the session, so events from inner pages still carry the click ID.
  • Phone numbers are normalised with a country code on both channels from one shared rule; a mismatch between browser and server hashing zeroes matching without any error.
  • fbp, fbc, IP and user agent are never hashed; email and phone are hashed on the server and passed in plain text to the pixel, which hashes them itself.
  • Contact clicks leave the page immediately, so server events are sent with navigator.sendBeacon and survive the unload.
  • A filled-in test event code sends your live conversions to the Test Events stream instead of your dataset. The panel flags it in red.
  • The access token is stored outside the settings array, is never printed on the front end, and can live in wp-config.php instead of the database.

Privacy

Nothing is sent to the plugin author. This plugin has no servers of its own,
no analytics of its own, no licence check and no usage reporting. The only
destinations it ever contacts are the advertising accounts the site owner
configures: Meta (Facebook), OpenAI (ChatGPT Ads) and Google — each only if the
site owner enters an ID for it.

The consent gate is on by default. On a fresh install the consent mode is
“strict”: no measurement script is loaded and no event is sent until the visitor
agrees. A built-in banner asks, unless one of the supported consent plugins is
detected, in which case that plugin’s decision is used. Turning the gate off is
an explicit choice the site owner has to make in the settings, and the settings
screen says what that means.

The visitor’s browser decides, not the server. The consent state is read in
the browser, so a cached page cannot serve one visitor’s decision to another.

The admin area is never measured. No event is sent from wp-admin, and by
default logged-in administrators, editors and shop managers are not measured on
the front end either.

What leaves the site, once configured and consented to: the event name, the
page URL, the visitor’s IP address and user agent, Meta’s own _fbp / _fbc
cookies, and — for form and order conversions — the email address, phone number,
name, city, postcode and country the visitor typed, SHA-256 hashed before they
leave the server. The site owner is the data controller for all of it.

External services

This plugin sends data to Meta (Facebook) and, if you configure them, to OpenAI and Google. Nothing is sent before you enter an ID.

Meta Conversions API (graph.facebook.com) — when you save a dataset ID and an access token, conversion events are sent from your server: event name, event time, page URL, the visitor’s IP address and user agent, the _fbp / _fbc cookies, and — for form and order conversions — the email address, phone number, name, city, postcode and country hashed with SHA-256 before they leave your site. Terms: https://www.facebook.com/legal/terms/businesstools — Privacy: https://www.facebook.com/privacy/policy

Meta Pixel (connect.facebook.net) — the pixel script is loaded in the visitor’s browser and reports the same events. Terms and privacy as above.

Meta pixel configuration (connect.facebook.net/signals/config/<id>) — read once every 12 hours in the admin area to detect event names Meta restricts on your pixel. No visitor data is sent.

The plugin also reads the site’s own home page once every six hours from the
admin area, to detect measurement tags installed by the theme or another plugin.
That request stays on the site’s own domain.

OpenAI Measurement Pixel (bzrcdn.openai.com, bzr.openai.com) — loaded in the visitor’s browser only if an OpenAI Pixel ID is saved, and only after marketing consent. It reports the same events and handles OpenAI’s own click identifier. Terms: https://openai.com/policies/advertising-terms/ — Privacy: https://openai.com/policies/

OpenAI Conversions API (bzr.openai.com/v1/events) — when an OpenAI Pixel ID and Conversions API key are saved, conversion events are sent from your server: event name, event time, page URL, the visitor’s IP address and user agent, OpenAI’s oppref and obref identifiers, and — for form and order conversions — the email address, phone number and name hashed with SHA-256, plus city, region, postcode and country as plain text, as OpenAI’s documentation specifies. The “Test server connection” button sends one event with validate_only, which OpenAI checks but does not save. Documentation: https://developers.openai.com/ads/conversions-api

Google (googletagmanager.com, google-analytics.com, googleadservices.com) — loaded in the visitor’s browser only if you enter a GA4, Google Tag Manager or Google Ads ID, and in the default strict consent mode only after the visitor agrees. In the optional Consent Mode v2 “advanced” setting they load before consent without writing cookies. It reports the page view and the conversions listed above; no data is sent from your server. Terms: https://policies.google.com/terms — Privacy: https://policies.google.com/privacy

plugins.name: Arrival for Woo
plugins.author: EMBARK STUDIO
plugins.short_description: The arrivals board for your Woo store — show shoppers exactly when orders arrive, with delivery dates, cutoff countdowns and free-shipping progress.
plugins.description:
Every shopper asks the same question: when will it get here?

Arrival reads your shipping zones, schedules and order cutoffs, then answers that question everywhere it matters — product page, cart, checkout — the way a board announces flights: a date, a time, a countdown. No guessing before the buy button. Fewer “do you deliver to…” emails. Fewer abandoned carts.

What the board shows

  • A real delivery date — “Get it by Wed 22 Jul”, calculated from your zones, schedule and cutoffs, shown on product pages, cart and checkout.
  • An order-cutoff countdown — “Order within 2 h 14 m” states the deadline as a fact, so urgency never has to shout.
  • Postcode-aware answers — shoppers enter their postcode once and see the methods, prices and dates that actually apply to them.
  • Free-shipping progress — “Add $7.20 more to unlock free delivery” builds baskets with information, not persuasion.
  • Cache-compatible behaviour — dynamic postcode and date messaging designed for real WooCommerce environments with page caching.

Why store owners install it

Clarity converts. When the answer to “when will it arrive?” is on the page, shoppers don’t leave to ask it by email — or leave for a store that answers it. Arrival exists to raise conversion, cut cart abandonment, and shrink your support inbox by moving fulfilment answers in front of the buy button.

Bricks Builder dynamic tags

  • {delivery_date} — calculated delivery date
  • {delivery_date:X} — delivery date with additional days
  • {delivery_location} — postcode display or entry prompt
  • {delivery_cutoff} — order cutoff countdown
  • {postcode_display} — plain-text postcode display
  • {order_delivery} — the estimate saved against a placed order (also {order_delivery:range} and {order_delivery:both})
  • {delivery_hours} / {pickup_hours} — opening hours for that channel

Shortcodes

  • [arwoo_calculator] — the full delivery board
  • [arwoo_delivery_date] — delivery date for the current postcode
  • [arwoo_delivery_cutoff] — cutoff countdown
  • [arwoo_postcode_display] — cache-compatible postcode display
  • [arwoo_delivery_location] — cache-compatible delivery location info
  • [arwoo_order_delivery] — the estimate saved against a placed order, for thank-you pages, emails and account pages
  • [arwoo_service_hours] — your opening hours, stated once and kept accurate (channel="pickup", format="list")

Arrival Pro — know when to arrive

Delivery tells shoppers when it lands. Pickup tells them when to arrive — and that’s what Arrival Pro adds:

  • Pickup readiness — “Ready from 16:40 · Open until 17:30”, aware of your store’s opening days and hours, so the trip is never a guess.
  • Unlimited pickup locations — multi-branch and multi-yard support.
  • Holidays — one-off closures the board respects automatically.
  • Recurring holidays — set Christmas once, forget it forever.
  • Custom styling — brand colours and CSS variables to match your storefront.
  • Google Places — address-assisted location entry.

Arrival Pro is sold separately at embark.studio. Everything described above the Pro section works in this free plugin, forever.

External services

plugins.name: TaxKeel – Tax Setup & Checker for WooCommerce
plugins.author: BrainFeed Solutions
plugins.short_description: Finds the mistakes in your WooCommerce tax setup - wrong rates, taxes that never apply, untaxed shipping - and fixes them in one click. Offline.
plugins.description:
“Taxes are not being calculated.” “WooCommerce is using the store address instead.” “The last update messed with my tax settings.” TaxKeel finds the setup mistakes behind these, explains each one in plain English, and fixes the ones that are safe to fix – with a preview first and one-click undo.

Tax set up right in 5 minutes, and kept right. No Jetpack, no subscription, no per-order fees.

The checker

TaxKeel runs 42 checks against your WooCommerce tax settings and rates. It asks WooCommerce’s own tax engine what a customer in each place would pay, so what it reports is what your checkout does. For example:

  • Taxes switched off while you have rates, or on with no rates at all
  • “Calculate tax based on” set to your shop address, so your other rates never apply
  • Rates that can never match: wrong country codes (UK instead of GB), province names instead of codes, a country in the city field, broken postcode ranges
  • Mistyped rates (0.2 instead of 20), duplicates, and rates that stack by mistake
  • Shipping not taxed where it normally is
  • Cached pages showing visitors someone else’s tax
  • Settings changed by a WooCommerce update – with a one-click restore
  • EU: out-of-date VAT rates (Estonia 24%, Romania 21%, Finland 25.5%…), EU countries missing a rate under OSS, the €10,000 OSS threshold, prices shown without VAT
  • Canada: Quebec QST set to compound (15.47% instead of 14.975%), Nova Scotia still at 15%, missing provinces, GST and QST merged into one line
  • Australia & New Zealand: wrong GST rate, prices shown without GST, the “incl. GST” label
  • US: state rates below the state rate, tax in states without sales tax, missing local rates
  • WooCommerce Tax: a broken Jetpack connection, and more than one tax service fighting over the same orders

Each issue shows what’s wrong, why it matters to your customers, the exact rows or settings behind it, and how we checked.

One-click fixes you can undo

Every fix shows a before-and-after preview. TaxKeel saves a snapshot of your tax settings and rates before changing anything, and every change can be undone from History. Nothing changes unless you click.

Setup wizard

Answer a few questions – where you’re based, where you’re registered – and TaxKeel sets up WooCommerce’s built-in tax for:

  • EU VAT, including OSS (destination VAT for all 27 countries) or home-country VAT under the threshold
  • UK VAT
  • Canada GST/HST, plus PST, RST or QST where you’re registered, as separate lines
  • Australian and New Zealand GST, including overseas sellers registered for low-value goods
  • US state base rates (with a clear note that local rates aren’t included)

You see every rate and setting on a review screen before anything is saved.

Kept right

TaxKeel checks again every week, after WooCommerce updates, and whenever tax settings change. It emails you only when it finds something new. It also warns you 30 days before a known rate change in a place you charge tax, such as Washington DC moving to 7% on 1 October 2026.

Private and offline

Rate data ships inside the plugin and is updated with plugin updates. TaxKeel makes no outside requests, needs no account, and sends nothing about your store anywhere.

Not tax advice

TaxKeel checks your WooCommerce tax setup against published rates and common configuration mistakes. It isn’t tax advice and can’t tell you what you owe or where you must register. Check with a tax professional.

TaxKeel Pro

TaxKeel Pro is an optional paid add-on (sold separately, with a 14-day free trial) that adds a past-order tax audit, bulk tax-class tools, a US economic nexus tracker, scheduled rate changes, an EU same-price mode, and agency reports. The free plugin stays fully functional without it and still makes no outside requests.

Import and export tax rates (CSV)

Import a tax rate CSV in WooCommerce’s own format – the file WooCommerce itself exports, or a paid US local-rate file – and every row is checked before anything is saved. Add new rates alongside your existing ones, or replace the rates for the countries, states and tax classes in the file (a country-wide row replaces every existing rate for that country and class; a file limited to specific states, like a California-only US local-rate file, leaves other states alone). One undoable import, shown in History like any other fix. Export all your tax classes to CSV in one file (WooCommerce’s own exporter does one class at a time).
